Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

text:
This looks like early 2014, probably February.

- Unemployment of 6.6% matches January 2014, when the rate was 6.6%.
- Fed funds at 0.07% and a 10-year yield of 2.65% fit that period.
- US large-cap equity returned 25.4% over 12 months, which fits the strong 2013 run.
- Gold was down 16.6% over 12 months, consistent with its 2013 decline, and the 1-month gain of 4.2% fits January 2014 gold, which rose.
- Equities gained 5.0% in the latest month. In January 2014 the S&P 500 fell about 3%, whereas February 2014 rose about 4.6%, which fits a February snapshot.
- Headline CPI of 1.56% year over year fits February 2014, when it was 1.1% in January and 1.1% in February by my recollection. Headline CPI rising 0.64 over three months is odd for that window. However, the 12-month and 3-month changes may be on a different basis than I remember.
- The 10-year yield was 2.65% at the end of February 2014 and 2.67% at the end of January. The 3-month change of −0.10 would then reference a November 2013 level of 2.75%, which fits.
- Unemployment fell 0.6 over three months. It was 7.2% in November 2013 (actually 7.0% in November and 6.7% in December), so the snapshot would put the latest month at 6.6% with February 2014 at 6.7%. January 2014 was 6.6%, so the data may be as of January, but the equity return points to February.

I'll go with February 2014.
